title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Defense to set up reporting rules for large AI contractors so they must share relevant data. It also calls for voluntary guidance to help these contractors use AI responsibly and align with defense priorities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 requires companies that design, deploy, or use AI systems to conduct formal risk assessments and submit their findings to a federal oversight body. The Act aims to promote transparency, safety, and accountability in AI development, ensuring technologies comply with ethical and legal standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is a proposed federal law that would create a coordinated public effort to explain what AI is and how it works. It aims to give people clear, accessible information about AI’s benefits, risks, and responsible use so they can make informed decisions.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence. The committee will be tasked with studying AI’s development, impact, and policy implications to guide legislative action.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill would help workers whose jobs are lost to automation or artificial intelligence by providing training programs and other support services. It also requires the federal government to take action during times of high unemployment and includes additional related provisions.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: This resolution highlights the Senate’s support for protecting religious freedom as artificial intelligence grows, stressing that faith-based values must be respected. It also calls for greater transparency in AI systems, urging that authoritative texts and principles guide their design and use.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee AI development and ensure its safe use. It also includes additional provisions to guide AI policy and regulation.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to safeguard people from misleading or deceptive use of artificial intelligence. It requires companies to clearly disclose when AI is involved and to prevent deceptive practices that could trick or harm consumers.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets out rules to make sure that AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and clearly explained. It requires researchers and developers to follow strict testing, documentation, and oversight procedures so that the public can have confidence in the technology.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy orders the Director of National Intelligence to send a report to Congress. The report will describe how artificial‑intelligence systems are used to collect, analyze, query, share, and otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to strengthen AI education at all levels so that the workforce is prepared for jobs that use AI. It provides funding and support for curriculum development, teacher training, and industry partnerships to build the necessary skills.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that encourages the creation and public sharing of AI tools and frameworks by offering funding, grants, or tax incentives to organizations that release their code openly. It also sets guidelines for transparency, safety, and collaboration so the United States can stay at the forefront of responsible open‑source AI innovation.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that only licensed medical professionals may provide diagnoses, prescriptions, and treatment plans, prohibiting AI systems from performing these tasks. It aims to protect patient safety by ensuring that medical care is delivered by qualified doctors, not automated algorithms.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is designed to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for their services and from engaging in practices that manipulate or suppress wages in the workforce. It aims to promote fair pricing, protect consumers and workers, and ensure a competitive AI market.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional provisions for related security measures, though the exact details are not specified.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate incidents related to cybersecurity and AI. It also includes additional provisions for related policy matters, though the specifics are not detailed in the title.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to finance AI research and development, fostering innovation and competitiveness. It also includes additional measures to promote responsible AI deployment and oversight.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a law that sets rules for creating, testing, and releasing artificial intelligence models so they are safe, reliable, and clear about what they can do. It requires companies to document their models, share how they work, and make sure they don’t cause harm or bias.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is proposed legislation that aims to shield households from the rising electricity bills generated by large AI data centers. It would likely introduce measures such as energy‑efficiency mandates, cost caps, or rebates to help families manage these increased energy expenses.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act establishes a new federal agency focused on coordinating AI research, development, and deployment. Its goal is to set national standards, promote responsible innovation, and ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI research and development. It also aims to establish regulations for advanced AI systems and addresses additional related matters.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is proposed legislation that seeks to guide the use of AI in services for veterans, ensuring the technology is safe, fair, and respects veterans’ privacy. It sets out standards for data protection, bias prevention, and accountability, and establishes oversight to safeguard veterans when AI is applied in healthcare, benefits, or other support programs.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes to curb the development and deployment of dangerous artificial intelligence systems that pose risks to public safety and national security. It seeks to establish stringent oversight, licensing, and accountability measures to prevent rogue AI from causing harm.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law designed to ensure that artificial intelligence used by the Department of Veterans Affairs in processing claims is transparent, fair, and accountable. It requires the VA to set clear AI guidelines, perform regular impact reviews, and give veterans understandable explanations and recourse for AI-driven decisions that affect their benefits.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a law that bans the use of certain artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to prevent the deployment of AI systems that could pose risks to public safety or privacy.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act requires defense agencies to rigorously test and certify AI systems to ensure they are safe and reliable before deployment. It also mandates regular reporting of AI performance and any incidents to oversight bodies, ensuring transparency and accountability.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to make AI tools used by the Department of Veterans Affairs more open and accountable. It requires the VA to disclose how AI systems are trained, what data they use, and how they influence decisions that affect veterans.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen the security of advanced artificial intelligence systems. It establishes guidelines and standards to protect AI technologies from threats and promote responsible use.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act aims to stop the use of artificial intelligence to automatically deny Medicare claims. It requires that any claim denial be reviewed by a human to ensure fairness and accuracy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily halt the construction and operation of new AI data centers, giving lawmakers time to assess their environmental, economic, and regulatory impacts. It aims to prevent rapid, unchecked expansion of energy‑intensive AI infrastructure while ensuring responsible development.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to protect AI models from unauthorized use and theft. It sets out penalties and safeguards to hold individuals and companies accountable for infringing on AI intellectual property rights in the United States.
